tool.name: RustScenic GRN
tool.description: infer TF-target networks from single-cell RNA expression
tool.command: #set $expression_path = 'expression.' + str($input.format) export RAYON_NUM_THREADS="\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" && export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 BLIS_NUM_THREADS=1 NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 && ln -s '${input.expression}' '$expression_path' && rustscenic grn --expression '$expression_path' --tfs '$tfs' --output 'grn.tsv' --seed '$seed' --n-estimators '$advanced.n_estimators' --learning-rate '$advanced.learning_rate' --max-features '$advanced.max_features' --subsample '$advanced.subsample' --max-depth '$advanced.max_depth' --early-stop-window '$advanced.early_stop_window' --early-stop-mode '$advanced.early_stop_mode'

tool.help:
Infer a weighted transcription-factor-to-target network from prepared single-cell RNA expression with RustScenic's histogram gradient-boosting implementation. The output contains candidate associations and is not experimental evidence of regulation or a motif-filtered regulon set.
Inputs ------
Use a cells-by-genes matrix of normalized, log-transformed RNA expression. This tool does not normalize, select genes or select an AnnData layer. For H5AD, place the intended expression in ``X`` and matching gene symbols in ``var_names``. For TSV/CSV, supply a header of gene symbols and cell IDs in the first column. The TF file contains one matching gene symbol per line. Blank lines and lines starting with ``#`` are ignored. At least one TF must match an expression gene.
The released CLI checks TF overlap against the input names before its inference code resolves alternative AnnData annotations. Put the intended symbols directly in ``var_names``; do not rely on a ``feature_name`` column to rescue an unmatched TF list. Inputs and the fitting matrix must fit the job's available memory.
Outputs -------
The **network** is a TSV with ``TF``, ``target`` and ``importance`` columns. Self-links and zero-importance edges are omitted by the upstream implementation. The **fitting metadata** is the upstream JSON containing version, seed, input dimensions, runtime and ``grn_fit`` settings/tree summaries. It does not contain input hashes or a complete software-environment record. Galaxy history retains the selected input datasets and tool parameters.
Fitting and interpretation --------------------------
The default early-stopping rule follows arboreto-style out-of-bag improvements; the historical in-bag rule is available for older RustScenic analyses. A zero window disables stopping. Setting the cell fraction to 1.0 leaves no out-of-bag cells, so the arboreto-style rule reaches the estimator ceiling. The random seed is recorded in the JSON; changes to data, parameters or implementation can alter the network.
RustScenic uses histogram-based boosting, while arboreto/pySCENIC uses scikit-learn models. Rankings and importance values can differ. This tool does not run GENIE3, motif filtering, AUCell or the complete SCENIC/SCENIC+ workflow. It makes no claim of output equivalence or biological validation. Galaxy's allocated CPU slots control Rayon parallelism; native numerical-library threads are limited to one to avoid nested parallelism.
See the `RustScenic documentation <https://ekin-kahraman.github.io/rustscenic/>`_ and `validation notes <https://ekin-kahraman.github.io/rustscenic/validation/>`_.
